about:
Lighthouse Woodworking was founded in 1995 by craftsman Ron Light in Boyce, Virginia. The shop began as a one-man operation focused on custom-built hardwood furniture, emphasizing a personal relationship between maker and client.

The company produces heirloom-quality pieces including bookcases, armoires, blanket chests, tables, and chairs using solid walnut, cherry, ash, and tiger maple. Each item is hand-crafted with traditional joinery such as through-dovetails, mortise-and-tenon, and custom crown molding. Finishes are hand-applied, often using Danish oil, and hardware ranges from soft-close Blum slides to handmade brass pulls. The workshop handles design, milling, assembly, and finishing in-house.

Lighthouse serves residential customers across Virginia, Pennsylvania, and surrounding regions. Clients include homeowners in Falls Church, Winchester, Woodbridge, Clarke County, Woodville, Round Hill, and Paris, Virginia, as well as Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. Projects range from single pieces like a pencil-post bed or Windsor chairs to whole-room systems such as a six-unit lighted shelf wall. The shop also restores and refinishes family heirlooms.

Light positions the business around a "custom furniture experience" where the client works directly with the craftsman from wood selection through final delivery. The company stresses affordably priced custom work, collaborative design, and attention to detail that ensures pieces become family heirlooms.
